items.name: adidas Junior F50 Messi Elite Firm Ground Soccer Cleats - El Ultimo Tango Pack (SP26)
items.description: Cada jugador joven tiene un favorito. Para muchos de ellos es Messi, y este es el puño que los pone en su línea. El junior F50 Messi es la firma de Messi F50, el zapato de velocidad de adidas cortado para un pie en crecimiento. Tu hijo no quiere un aspecto parecido. Quieren la verdadera firma Messi. Esta es la construcción Elite de la adidas F50. La parte superior de Hybridtouch+ da un toque limpio y suave, con un Halocage+ Piel TPU colocada donde un jugador empuja hacia fuera para cortes rápidos. La placa F50 Speedsystem funciona de longitud completa con estrías afiladas, para agarre y accionamiento cuando se plantan y corren sobre pasto seco. A 5,5 oz (156 g) en el tamaño inferior, apenas hay nada en su pie. La ruta de color El Ultimo Tango corre Marfil con Semi Blue Burst e Icey Blue. Para un jugador en desarrollo en hierba firme, esto es un montón de cleat escalado para caber. ¿Quieres más? Examine la colección de correas de velocidad adidas F50. Detalles del producto: F50 Messi Elite Tier: Elite, la construcción F50 de alto nivel, tamaño junior Signature: Messi F50 line, El Ultimo Tango pack Upper: Hybridtouch+ sintético con una Halocage+ de precisión TPU piel para cortes rápidos Placa: F50 Speedsystem TPU de longitud completa con estrías afiladas, terreno firme (FG) Sockliner: LIGHTSTRIKEPRO para amortiguación ligera Peso: 5,5 oz (156 g) en el tamaño junior Colorway: Marfil / Semi Blue Burst / Icey Blue Fit: ajuste regular con un cierre de encaje Fit Notes El F50 Messi corre un junior regular ajustado con un cierre de encaje estándar, por lo que la mayoría de los niños consiguen un mango ajustado y seguro fiel al tamaño. Cuidado y mantenimiento Aire seco después
items.description_en: Every young player has a favorite. For a lot of them it's Messi, and this is the cleat that puts them in his line. The junior F50 Messi is Messi's signature F50, adidas's speed shoe cut down for a growing foot. Your kid doesn't want a look-alike. They want the real Messi signature. This is the Elite build of the adidas F50. The Hybridtouch+ upper gives a clean, soft touch, with a Halocage+ TPU skin placed where a player pushes off for quick cuts. The F50 Speedsystem plate runs full-length with bladed studs, for grip and drive when they plant and sprint on dry grass. At 5.5 oz (156 g) in the junior size, there's barely anything on their foot. The El Ultimo Tango colorway runs Ivory with Semi Blue Burst and Icey Blue. For a developing player on firm grass, this is a lot of cleat scaled to fit. Want more? Browse the adidas F50 speed cleats collection. Product Details: F50 Messi Elite Tier: Elite, the top-tier F50 build, junior sizing Signature: Messi F50 line, El Ultimo Tango pack Upper: Hybridtouch+ synthetic with a precision-placed Halocage+ TPU skin for quick cuts Plate: F50 Speedsystem full-length TPU with bladed studs, firm ground (FG) Sockliner: LIGHTSTRIKEPRO for lightweight cushioning Weight: 5.5 oz (156 g) in the junior size Colorway: Ivory / Semi Blue Burst / Icey Blue Fit: regular fit with a lace closure Fit Notes The F50 Messi runs a regular junior fit with a standard lace closure, so most kids get a snug, secure hold true to size. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture out Keep them off direct heat, sunlight, and the dryer, which warp the plate and dry out the upper Brush off dried grass and dirt before storing The Hybridtouch+ synthetic upper needs only a soft brush and a damp wipe, no leather conditioner Store somewhere cool and dry, not a hot car or a closed bag FAQs about the F50 Messi Elite Is this a real Messi cleat or just a Messi look? It's the real F50 Messi, the Elite build of the F50 speed line Messi wears, in the El Ultimo Tango colorway and junior sizing. What surface are these built for? Firm ground (FG), meaning dry natural grass. The bladed studs suit firm pitches, not turf or soft, muddy fields. My kid is growing fast. Should I size up? They run true to size in a regular junior fit. Between sizes or mid-growth-spurt, a half size up buys room while keeping the hold secure.

items.name: Nike Junior Phantom 6 Low Pro NU3 Firm/Multi Ground Soccer Cleats - United NU3 Pack (SU26)
items.description: El cleat para la temporada todo comienza a hacer clic en En algún lugar entre la pelota de rec y los partidos reales, un jugador joven deja de patear y comienza a colocarla. El pase encuentra a un compañero a propósito. El disparo va hacia donde significaban que iba. El Nike Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro está construido para exactamente ese estiramiento, cuando el tacto y el control comienzan a importar más que cualquier otra cosa en el campo. Esta es la línea de control Phantom, tamaño para el crecimiento de pies y precio para un niño que ha ganado el paso hacia arriba sin necesidad de la recepción de nivel superior. Grippy VNMSkin cubre el área llamativa para toques más limpios en la bola, y el Flyknit de Nike trabaja debajo de ella para acercar el pie al balón. El marco del zapato moldea alrededor del pie para un ajuste natural, más espacioso a través de la caja del dedo, que importa cuando los pies todavía están creciendo y un ajuste ajustado-pero-no-tight mantiene a un niño cómodo a través de un partido completo. Construido para ir a cualquier lugar del fin de semana, la mayoría de los tacos junior eligen una superficie y paran allí. La placa firme/multi-ground en el Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro es la opción do-it-all: agarra césped natural firme para el club del sábado, y se mantiene en las superficies más difíciles, parcheteros que un jugador joven corre en la escuela y en el parque. Un patrón de tracción Cyclone 360 de pie les ayuda a plantar y pivotar cuando se cortan. Un par, la mayoría de las superficies en las que juega un jugador en crecimiento, lo que es una cosa menos para averiguar antes de la patada. Para una visión más amplia de la línea de control, la colección Nike Phantom lleva a la familia a través de los niveles y tamaños.
items.description_en: The cleat for the season it all starts to click Somewhere between rec ball and real matches, a young player stops just kicking it and starts placing it. The pass finds a teammate on purpose. The shot goes where they meant it to go. The Nike Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro is built for exactly that stretch, when touch and control start to matter more than anything else on the pitch. This is the Phantom control line, sized for growing feet and priced for a kid who has earned the step up without needing the top-tier receipt. Grippy VNMSkin covers the striking area for cleaner touches on the ball, and Nike's Flyknit works underneath it to bring the foot closer to the ball. The shoe frame molds around the foot for a natural fit, roomier through the toe box, which matters when feet are still growing and a snug-but-not-tight fit keeps a kid comfortable through a full match. Built to go anywhere the weekend does Most junior cleats pick one surface and stop there. The firm/multi-ground plate on the Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro is the do-it-all option: it grips firm natural grass for Saturday club, and it holds up on the harder, patchier surfaces a young player runs into at school and at the park. A forefoot Cyclone 360 traction pattern helps them plant and pivot when they cut. One pair, most of the surfaces a growing player actually plays on, which is one less thing to figure out before kickoff. For a wider look at the control line, the Nike Phantom collection carries the family across tiers and sizes. Who it's for This one fits the developing youth player who's outgrown a first pair of basic cleats and wants gear that matches the touch they've built. The low-cut collar keeps things light and free at the ankle, so a kid gets quick release without extra bulk. It sits in the Pro tier of Nike's junior line, a real step up from entry-level cleats without the flagship price. If you're comparing options across price points for a growing player, the full Nike soccer cleat range lays out the tiers side by side. Product Details: Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro Nike VNMSkin over the striking area for grip and control on dribbles, passes, and shots Flyknit underlay to bring the foot closer to the ball Molded shoe frame for a natural fit with a roomier toe box Firm/multi-ground (FMG) plate for firm natural grass plus harder and mixed surfaces Forefoot Cyclone 360 circular traction pattern for planting and pivoting Low-cut collar for a light, free ankle Junior Pro tier; part of the Nike United NU3 Pack (SU26), Burgundy Crush/University Red with animal-print graphics Youth sizing 2 to 5.5 Fit Notes The Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro runs true to size for most young players, with a slightly roomier toe box than Nike's speed lines. If your kid has a wider foot or is between sizes with a growth spurt coming, the natural-fit frame gives a little breathing room without going sloppy. When you can, have them try cleats on later in the day, when feet are at their largest. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them away from direct heat, sunlight, and the dryer, which breaks down the upper and warps the plate Brush off dried grass and dirt with a soft brush before storing The synthetic VNMSkin and Flyknit upper needs no conditioner, just a soft brush and a wipe with a damp cloth Store at room temperature, not in a hot car or a cold garage FAQs about the Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro Does the Jr Phantom 6 Low Pro run true to size? It runs true to size for most young players, with a slightly roomier toe box than Nike's speed cleats. For a wider foot or a growth spurt on the way, the natural-fit frame leaves a little room without feeling loose. What surfaces can my kid play on in these? The firm/multi-ground (FMG) plate is the versatile one. It grips firm natural grass for club matches and holds up on the harder, mixed surfaces at school and the park. It is not built for dedicated artificial-turf carpets or indoor courts; those need AG or IC cleats. What is the difference between the Low Pro and the Academy junior versions? The Low Pro sits in the Pro tier with the VNMSkin control upper and the molded shoe frame, a real step up in touch and feel. The Academy versions are the more entry-level junior tier at a lower price. If your player is getting serious about control, the Low Pro is the upgrade. Is this a good first serious cleat for a developing player? Yes. It brings Phantom control to junior feet at a Pro-tier level without the flagship price, and the FMG plate covers most of the surfaces a growing player runs into week to week.

items.name: Nike Tiempo Maestro Academy Turf Soccer Shoes - Breakout Pack (SU26)
items.description: cuero suave, tacto real, hecho para césped Los mejores jugadores de césped no disparan la pelota, lo resuelven. La Academia Nike Tiempo Maestro es el zapato de cuero suave para ese jugador en césped artificial: el juego de recreo de la semana y la práctica larga. Su parte superior de cuero FlyTouch es genuinamente suave, por lo que la pelota se sienta donde la pones en lugar de rebotar un sintético rígido. Por qué FlyTouch piel se siente rota en el día uno zapatos Stiff te castigan por las dos primeras semanas. El cuero FlyTouch va por el otro lado. Es ligero y moldes a su pie sin sobrecarga, por lo que se siente cómodo temprano y da un toque consistente si el césped es seco o deslizante con rocío. Menos tiempo rompiéndolos, más tiempo jugando. Quien el zapato de césped Tiempo Maestro Academy es para Este es para el turf regular que quiere una sensación de cuero real sin un precio de elite-tier. Zapatos de césped (TF) están hechos para césped artificial y astroturf antiguo, con una suela de goma plana en lugar de estrías, por lo que consigue agarre sin la captura que da un puño firme. Si usted está pesando los niveles, la gama completa Tiempo Maestro va desde esta construcción de entrada a la Elite, y el resto del paquete Breakout comparte la apariencia. Detalles del producto: Tiempo Maestro Academy Turf FlyTouch leather upper: soft and lightweight, mold to the foot for a consistent touch in wet or dry conditions Rubber outsole and turf (TF) build for traction on artificial turf and older astroturf Low-profile turf silhouette, part of Nike Tiempo touch-and-control line Acad
items.description_en: Soft leather, real touch, made for turf The best turf players don't blast the ball, they settle it. The Nike Tiempo Maestro Academy is the soft-leather shoe for that player on artificial turf: the weeknight rec game and the long practice. Its FlyTouch leather upper is genuinely soft, so the ball sits where you put it instead of bouncing off a stiff synthetic. Why FlyTouch leather feels broken in on day one Stiff shoes punish you for the first two weeks. The FlyTouch leather here goes the other way. It's lightweight and molds to your foot without overstretching, so it feels comfortable early and gives a consistent touch whether the turf is dry or slick with dew. Less time breaking them in, more time playing. Who the Tiempo Maestro Academy turf shoe is for This one's for the turf regular who wants real leather feel without an elite-tier price. Turf shoes (TF) are made for artificial turf and older astroturf, with a flat rubber outsole instead of studs, so you get grip without the catch a firm-ground cleat gives. If you're weighing the tiers, the full Tiempo Maestro range runs from this entry build to the Elite, and the rest of the Breakout pack shares the look. Product Details: Tiempo Maestro Academy Turf FlyTouch leather upper: soft and lightweight, molds to the foot for a consistent touch in wet or dry conditions Rubber outsole and turf (TF) build for traction on artificial turf and older astroturf Low-profile turf silhouette, part of Nike's Tiempo touch-and-control line Academy tier: Nike's accessible build below the Pro and Elite Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack, SU26) Fit Notes The Maestro Academy runs true to size for most players. The soft FlyTouch leather gives a little, so if you're between sizes or have a wider foot, it forgives that better than a stiff synthetic. Try them on with your game socks. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every session; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them away from direct heat and dryers, which dry out the leather Brush off turf pellets and dried dirt before storing Wipe with a damp cloth; condition lightly if the leather stiffens FAQs about the Tiempo Maestro Academy Turf Where can I wear the Tiempo Maestro Academy turf shoe? On artificial turf and older astroturf. The flat rubber outsole grips the synthetic surface without the studs you'd want on natural grass, so keep your firm-ground (FG) cleats for the grass field and use these on turf. What's the difference between the Academy and Elite Tiempo Maestro? Both sit in Nike's Tiempo touch-and-control line, but the Academy is the accessible entry build and the Elite is the top tier, with premium materials and a higher price. The Academy still gives you soft FlyTouch leather for real ball feel, which is the whole point of the Tiempo line. Does the Tiempo Maestro Academy run true to size? Yes, true to size for most players. The soft FlyTouch leather molds to your foot, so if you're between sizes or run wide it gives a little more than a stiff synthetic would. Try them on with your match socks. Is real leather worth it on a turf shoe? If you care about your first touch, yes. Soft leather wraps the ball better than hard plastic, and the FlyTouch upper stays light enough that you don't trade away comfort for feel. That touch is what the Tiempo Maestro is known for, and you get it here at an entry price.

items.description_en: Midweek turf is where cheap shoes give up You know the pattern. A pair looks fine in September and is splitting by November. The Phantom 6 Low Academy is built for the sessions between game days, the ones that quietly do the damage. Nike didn't cut the touch zone here NikeSkin sits over engineered mesh across the forefoot, and the expanded touch zone shows up on every pass. Wet or dry, the ball comes off the same. It links this pair to the wider Nike Phantom range . One surface, done properly Turf chews through the wrong outsole. This one is rubber, set up for quick traction on artificial surfaces, which is where the midweek sessions usually land. If the season also runs on grass, the firm and multi ground version covers that. Product Details: Phantom 6 Low Academy Turf Upper: engineered mesh with an expanded NikeSkin touch zone Outsole: rubber, built for quick traction on turf Surface: artificial turf, training and small-sided games Cut: low, Academy tier Colorway: Breakout Pack (SU26) Fit Notes The frame shapes around the foot with room through the front, which helps when toes are still growing. Runs true to size, so leave about a thumb's width at the end. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every session, newspaper inside pulls the moisture out No radiators, no car heaters, no dryers Brush the turf pellets off before they pack in A soft brush and a damp cloth handle the mesh upper FAQs about the Phantom 6 Low Academy Turf Can these be worn on natural grass? They're turf shoes, so the outsole is set up for artificial surfaces. For grass, take the firm and multi ground version in the same Breakout Pack. What does the Academy tier get you? Indoor courts need a flat sole.

items.description_en: One pair for grass and the field behind the school Most kids don't get one surface. They get the good pitch on match day and whatever's left the rest of the week. One pair covers both. A soft upper and a collar that stays put The upper is a malleable material that moves with the foot, so there's no stiff break-in stretch. The knit cuff keeps the ankle from sliding. Compare tiers across the Nike Phantom range . Firm ground and multi ground, without the jargon Firm ground (FG) studs suit natural grass. Multi ground (MG) studs handle mixed and harder fields. This plate does both. If the league plays mostly on old astroturf, the turf version from the same Breakout Pack is the smarter buy. Product Details: Phantom 6 High Club Malleable upper that molds to the foot High-cut knit cuff for a locked-in ankle Firm ground and multi ground (FG/MG) outsole for grass and mixed fields Traction pattern built for quick direction changes Foot-shaped frame with room up front Breakout Pack (SU26) colorway Fit Notes Runs true to size for most players. The cuff is snug on purpose, so point the toe and pull it on. Wider feet are usually happier a half size up. Care and Maintenance Brush dried grass and dirt off after every match Air-dry away from heaters, dryers and direct sun Newspaper inside holds the shape while they dry Never machine wash or tumble dry them Pull the insoles out between matches; that's what kills the smell FAQs about the Phantom 6 High Club Can my kid wear these on artificial turf? Occasional games on newer artificial grass are fine. A full season on older turf calls for a turf shoe. Is the high collar hard to pull on? The knit cuff stretches. Point the toe and open it with both hands, like a sock. Are these a good first pair of cleats? Yes. Club is the entry tier, the plate covers grass and mixed fields, and there's no break-in to sit through.

items.name: Nike Zoom Superfly 11 Pro Firm Ground Soccer Cleats - Breakout Pack (SU26)
items.description: Construido para la carrera de pie de treinta metros Estás nivelado a diez metros, la pelota en el canal y un escalón defensor para zancada. El Nike Mercurial Superfly 11 Pro está construido para lo que viene a continuación: la mitad trasera de ese sprint, donde el jugador más rápido se despeja. Este es el Mercurial de alta calidad, hecho para los jugadores que ganan juegos en espacio abierto. Cuando se abra el carril, tómalo. Lo que hace que la línea Mercurial de Superfly 11 Pro rápido Nike ha tenido un trabajo durante años: hacer los atacantes rápido más rápido. El Superfly 11 Pro lleva esa línea de velocidad en el nivel Pro, un paso por debajo del paquete despojado de Elite pero sintonizado para el mismo juego de línea recta. Una unidad de zoom de aire primavera bajo el pie envía cada empuje de regreso a su zancada. La parte superior FlyWeave envuelve fino y estrecho en el Multi-Color/Black del paquete Breakout, bloqueando el pie hacia arriba. Se encuentra en el centro de la línea de liberación de Nike, la velocidad Mercurial se siente a un precio accesible. Quien el Mercurial Superfly 11 Pro es para Este es para el comerciante de velocidad. Si su juego es la carrera detrás, la superposición por el flanco, la recuperación sprint-side, el Superfly 11 Pro se ajusta a cómo se juega. El cuello de corte alto envuelve el tobillo y te mantiene encerrado en el tono completo, donde un corte bajo deja flotar el pie. Los fans de Mercurial de largo tiempo obtienen la mirada y el linaje; los jugadores competitivos obtienen un juego de velocidad real que pueden permitirse. Si su juego es de control cercano en bolsillos apretados, el bajo corte Nike Vapor 17 Pro es el mejor partido. Detalles del producto: Superfly 11 Pro Fl
items.description_en: Built for the thirty-yard foot race You're level at ten yards, the ball into the channel and a defender stride for stride. The Nike Mercurial Superfly 11 Pro is built for what comes next: the back half of that sprint, where the fastest player pulls clear. This is the high-cut Mercurial, made for players who win games in open space. When the lane opens, take it. What makes the Superfly 11 Pro fast Nike's Mercurial line has had one job for years: make fast attackers faster. The Superfly 11 Pro carries that speed lineage at the Pro tier, a step below the Elite's stripped-back package but tuned for the same straight-line game. A springy Air Zoom unit under the forefoot sends every push-off back into your stride. The FlyWeave upper wraps thin and close in the Breakout pack's Multi-Color/Black, locking the foot down at top gear. It sits in the middle of Nike's cleat lineup , the Mercurial speed feel at a reachable price. Who the Mercurial Superfly 11 Pro is for This one is for the speed merchant. If your game is the run in behind, the overlap down the flank, the recovery sprint goal-side, the Superfly 11 Pro fits how you play. The high-cut collar wraps the ankle and keeps you locked in at full stride, where a low-cut lets the foot float. Longtime Mercurial fans get the look and the lineage; competitive players get a real speed cleat they can afford. If your game is close control in tight pockets, the low-cut Nike Vapor 17 Pro is the better match. Product Details: Superfly 11 Pro FlyWeave upper for a tailored, locked-in fit Air Zoom unit in the forefoot for a responsive, springy step High-cut collar, the signature Superfly silhouette Chevron studs for grip and sharp direction changes Firm ground (FG) plate for natural grass and dry surfaces Colorway: Multi-Color/Black, Breakout pack (SU26) Fit Notes The Superfly 11 Pro runs snug and streamlined, true to the Mercurial speed fit. Most players can order their normal size. If you have a wider foot, consider going up a half size. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them away from direct heat, sunlight, and dryers, which warp the plate Brush off dried grass and dirt with a soft brush before storing The synthetic FlyWeave upper needs no conditioner, just a wipe-down FAQs about the Superfly 11 Pro What is the difference between the Superfly 11 Pro and the Superfly 11 Elite? Both are high-cut Mercurial speed cleats. The Elite is the stripped-back flagship with Nike's top-end build; the Pro keeps the same speed shape and the Air Zoom forefoot unit at a lower price, making it the value pick for players who want the Mercurial feel without the flagship cost. Should I get the Superfly or the Vapor? They are the two halves of the Mercurial line. The Superfly is high-cut and built for straight-line, top-end speed. The Vapor is low-cut and tuned for close control and quick changes of direction in tight space. Pick the Superfly if your game is the run in behind; pick the Vapor if it is beating players one-on-one. What surface are these cleats made for? The firm ground (FG) plate is built for natural grass and dry, well-maintained surfaces. For dedicated artificial grass, look at the AG version instead, which carries a stud pattern designed for synthetic turf. Do the Superfly 11 Pro run true to size? They run snug and streamlined, the standard Mercurial speed fit. Most players can order their usual size. If you have a wider foot, going up a half size will give you more room.

items.description: Top-End Speed, Refinado para césped artificial Piense en un sprinter que pasó años en una pista de cinder, luego se cambió a uno sintético. Las mismas piernas, el mismo paso, la misma patada final. La superficie cambió, así que los picos cambiaron, y la velocidad se llevó directamente. Eso es lo que hace el Nike Superfly 11 Elite en césped artificial. La línea Mercurial es la más rápida de Nike, los defensores de la persecución Mbappe y Ronaldo, y esta es la versión diseñada para la alfombra verde en la que juega tu liga. Todavía tienes el primer paso explosivo. Sólo tienes que ponerlo en la superficie bajo tus pies. Por qué la placa AG-Pro morde la superficie sintética Cualquier persona que haya jugado en 3G conoce el miedo: se plantan para cortar, y el cleat se desliza medio pie antes de que se captura. La placa AG-Pro lo arregla. Sus sementales están huecos para que se agarren más fuerte, césped sintético más denso en lugar de esquiar por la parte superior, y hay más sementales a través del descalzo para que pueda cambiar el ritmo de carrera y confiar en sus pies para sostener. Si observas la brecha, te alejas, y el suelo te da la energía que pones. Esa confianza para comprometerse plenamente es el punto completo de los zapatos de fútbol artificiales hechos para el trabajo. Encerrado en Full Pace Speed es inútil si tu pie se mueve por dentro del cleat. La parte superior FlyWeave Ultra envuelve el pie de talón a dedo para una sujeción a medida, y bajo el descalzo la unidad Air Zoom y la espuma ZoomX le dan el rendimiento energético más alto de Nike, por lo que cada zancada se rompe. items.description_en: Top-End Speed, Re-Tuned for Artificial Grass Think of a sprinter who spent years on a cinder track, then switched to a synthetic one. Same legs, same stride, same finishing kick. The surface changed, so the spikes changed, and the speed carried straight over. That's what the Nike Superfly 11 Elite does on artificial grass. The Mercurial line is Nike's fastest, the cleat Mbappe and Ronaldo chase defenders in, and this is the version engineered for the green carpet your league actually plays on. You still get the explosive first step. You just get it on the surface under your feet. Why the AG-Pro Plate Bites the Synthetic Surface Anyone who's played on 3G knows the fear: you plant to cut, and the cleat slides half a foot before it catches. The AG-Pro plate fixes that. Its studs are hollowed out so they grip harder, denser synthetic turf instead of skidding across the top, and there are extra studs across the forefoot so you can change pace mid-run and trust your feet to hold. You spot the gap, you push off, and the ground gives you back the energy you put in. That confidence to commit fully is the whole point of artificial grass soccer cleats made for the job. Locked In at Full Pace Speed is useless if your foot moves around inside the cleat. The FlyWeave Ultra upper wraps your foot from heel to toe for a tailored hold, and under the forefoot the Air Zoom unit and ZoomX foam give you Nike's highest energy return, so every stride snaps back. This is the High collar, so the Dynamic Fit cuff seals your ankle and keeps everything connected through hard cuts. Want the same speed on dry natural grass instead? Check the Superfly 11 in the Nike Mercurial collection . Product Details AG-Pro outsole: studs hollowed out for grip on harder, synthetic surfaces, with extra forefoot studs for confident speed changes Air Zoom forefoot unit plus ZoomX foam underneath for Nike's highest energy return FlyWeave Ultra upper woven from heel to toe for a tailored, secure lockdown High Dynamic Fit collar for a sealed, locked-in ankle at top pace Elite tier: Nike's top-level Mercurial Superfly build Surface: artificial grass (AG-Pro plate) Colorway: Breakout Pack (SU26) FAQs About Nike Zoom Superfly 11 Elite AG Cleats These are AG cleats. Can I wear them on natural grass or turf? They're built for artificial grass, the dense synthetic surface a lot of clubs train and play on now. You can wear them on dry natural grass in a pinch, but the AG-Pro studs are shaped to bite synthetic, so on real grass, you lose a little of that grip. For natural grass, the Superfly 11 Elite FG is the match; for old-school rubber-pellet turf, look at a TF version instead. Does the Superfly 11 Elite AG run true to size? For most players, true to size. The FlyWeave Ultra upper is a snug, speed-fit cleat by design, so if you have a wider forefoot or wear thick game socks, try it on with those socks before you commit. The fitting room in Pasadena is open until 8 pm if you want to size it in person. Is the high collar worth it, or should I get the low-cut? The high collar is a feel preference, not a performance must. The Dynamic Fit cuff seals your ankle and gives you a connected, locked-in sensation through cuts, which a lot of speed players love. If you don't like anything wrapping your ankle, the low-cut Superfly gives you the same plate and upper without the collar. Superfly or Vapor for a winger on artificial grass? Both are Mercurial speed cleats, but they feel different. The Vapor 17 is more minimal and barefoot-light for instant separation. The Superfly adds the Air Zoom unit and a more structured upper, so it's a touch heavier but returns more energy on repeated sprints. If your game is sustained, repeated attacking down the flank, the Superfly is the pick.

items.description_en: Nike Mercurial Vapor 17 Pro FG Soccer Cleats Some players need a runway. You don't. Your game lives in the tight stuff, the touch-and-turn that leaves a marker grabbing at air. The Mercurial Vapor 17 Pro is the cleat for that player. It's the low-cut Vapor, tuned for quickness in close, not straight-line speed, and the Pro gives you most of the Elite's game for less. Nike's Mad Quick lane, built into the cleat Nike split the Mercurial into two lanes, and the Vapor owns the Mad Quick side, where the game is played in tight space. The Superfly chases straight-line speed; the Vapor lives in the cut. The Pro keeps that low-cut Vapor identity with a full Flyknit upper that wraps the foot like a sock, and a friendlier fit than the Elite's stripped-back AtomKnit. Same agility DNA, in the Breakout Pack's Multi-Color and black for the summer matches of the 2026 cycle. The pickpocket's first touch Think of a pickpocket in a crowd. Quick hands, a touch you never see coming, and the ball's gone the other way. That's this cleat in a packed midfield. The Flyknit upper keeps your touch close, the thin plate snaps you out of the turn, and the chevron studs bite firm grass when you plant and cut. That's the edge in tight space, the half-yard that turns a crowded pocket into a clear path. Product Details Flyknit upper for a lightweight, sock-like wrap that brings your foot close to the ball Low-cut Vapor silhouette tuned for quick feet and change of direction in tight spaces Thin, lightweight outsole plate that adds responsiveness and snap on each step Chevron studs and a firm-ground (FG) outsole for start-stop traction on dry natural grass Pro tier: most of the Elite's Vapor agility package with a more forgiving fit and accessible price Synthetic lining and outsole; lace closure for a locked-in fit Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack) Fit Notes The Vapor runs narrow to standard and true to size for most players. The Pro's full Flyknit upper gives a touch more room than the Elite's AtomKnit, friendlier for a medium-width foot. Narrow feet lock in at the standard size; wider feet may want a half size up. Sizing runs in combined men's and women's increments (M 4 / W 5.5 and up), so check the size chart. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to hold the shape Keep them away from heat, sun, and the dryer, which break down the Flyknit and warp the plate Brush off dried grass before storing; the synthetic Flyknit needs only a soft brush Store at room temperature, not a hot trunk or a damp gym bag FAQs about Nike Vapor 17 Pro FG Cleats Does the Vapor 17 Pro run true to size? It runs true to size for most players. The Vapor is a narrow-to-standard cleat, and the Pro's full Flyknit upper sits a little more forgiving than the Elite's AtomKnit. If your foot is narrow you'll lock in at your standard size; if it's wider, go up a half size for a bit more room. What's the difference between the Vapor 17 Pro and the Elite? Both are the low-cut Vapor built for quickness in tight spaces. The Elite uses Nike's lightest AtomKnit upper and FlyLite plate for the most stripped-back, near-barefoot feel, and it's the priciest tier. The Pro keeps the same Vapor agility identity with a full Flyknit upper, a sock-like wrap, and a slightly more forgiving fit, for a good bit less money. If you want the Vapor game without the Elite spend, the Pro is the one. Should I get the Vapor or the Superfly? Pick the Vapor if your game is quick feet in close: the touch out of pressure, the chop inside, the sharp cut before a shot. The Superfly leans toward straight-line acceleration and repeat sprints down the line. Both are Mercurials; the Vapor is the Mad Quick one. You can see the full lineup on the Nike Mercurial collection . Are these cleats good for turf or artificial grass? No, these are firm-ground (FG) cleats made for dry natural grass. The chevron stud pattern is built to bite real grass and can feel harsh on turf or artificial surfaces. If you play mostly on those, look for the turf or AG version instead. The rest of this drop lives on the Breakout Pack collection .

items.name: Nike Vapor 17 Elite Firm Ground Soccer Cleats - Breakout Pack (SU26)
items.description: Nike Vapor 17 Elite FG: El Burst que gana en los espacios de visión Tienes la pelota con la espalda a la meta, un marcador respirando sobre ti y sin espacio para girar. Luego te conviertes, una pintura rápida, un toque en la brecha, y te has ido antes de que el defensor lo lea. Ese medio segundo es por lo que vive el Nike Mercurial Vapor 17 Elite FG. Es la línea de agilidad de la familia Mercurial de Nike, la puntera baja para el alambrador que corta dentro y el número diez bailando a través de un campo medio lleno. Donde la Superfly persigue la velocidad de línea recta por el canal, el Vapor es para el jugador que golpea a la gente en un patio de césped. Por qué AtomKnit mantiene la pelota en tu pie Golpear a un defensor uno-a-uno es el trabajo de pie, de la misma manera un boxeador se desliza un golpe: pequeñas manchas, pies rápidos, y un toque en el que confías sin mirar hacia abajo. La parte superior de AtomKnit te da ese toque. Es el Flyknit más ligero y delgado de Nike, una capa de pies cercanos que envuelve el pie para que la pelota se siente más cerca de tu piel a través de cada corte rápido. Siente la pelota, no el embrague, que es exactamente lo que quieres cuando la obra sucede en un patio de espacio y no hay tiempo para arreglarla. Luz construida para cambios de tierra firme y dirección rápida La placa FG está hecha para césped natural firme y seco, la mayoría de clubes y escuelas juegan en. Bajo el descalzo, el peso de las tiras de placas ultra-thin FlyLite y te introduce en la siguiente dirección, y la mordedura de estrías de chevron para que puedas plantar y pivotar sin deslizarse. Todo el cleat está despojado de vuelta a casi nada.
items.description_en: Nike Vapor 17 Elite FG: The Burst That Wins in Tight Spaces You get the ball with your back to goal, a marker breathing on you and no room to turn. Then you do turn, one quick feint, a touch into the gap, and you're gone before the defender reads it. That half-second is what the Nike Mercurial Vapor 17 Elite FG lives for. It's the agility line in Nike's Mercurial family, the low-cut cleat for the winger cutting inside and the number ten dancing through a crowded midfield. Where the Superfly chases straight-line speed down the channel, the Vapor is for the player who beats people in a yard of grass. Why AtomKnit Keeps the Ball on Your Foot Beating a defender one-on-one is footwork, the same way a boxer slips a punch: small feints, fast feet, and a touch you trust without looking down. The AtomKnit upper gives you that touch. It's Nike's lightest, thinnest Flyknit ever, a near-barefoot layer that wraps the foot so the ball sits closer to your skin through every quick cut. You feel the ball, not the cleat, which is exactly what you want when the play happens in a yard of space and there's no time to settle it. Built Light for Firm Ground and Fast Direction Changes The FG plate is made for firm, dry natural grass, the pitch most clubs and schools play on. Under the forefoot, the ultra-thin FlyLite plate strips weight and snaps you into the next direction, and the chevron studs bite so you can plant and pivot without sliding. The whole cleat is stripped back to almost nothing, which is the point: less weight, faster feet, a sharper change of direction. Want the speed build instead of the agility build? Compare the line in the Nike Mercurial collection . Product Details AtomKnit upper: Nike's lightest, most transparent Flyknit, for a near-barefoot ball feel close to the foot FlyLite plate: ultra-thin lightweight plate that cuts weight and adds snap for fast acceleration and direction change Chevron stud pattern for grip, sharp pivots, and stop-on-a-dime cuts Low-cut collar for a natural ankle range through quick changes of direction Up to the lightest Mercurial build to date at the Elite tier Firm-ground (FG) outsole for dry natural grass Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack, SU26) Elite tier: Nike's top-level Vapor build FAQs About Nike Vapor 17 Elite AG Cleats The Vapor 17 is a low-cut cleat. How does the fit run? For most players, true to size, with a snug, sock-like AtomKnit fit through the midfoot. It's a low collar, so there's no ankle sleeve to size around; you just get a close, locked-down feel. If you have a wider forefoot or wear thick game socks, try them on with those, and if you're truly between sizes the snug knit means you can usually stay at your normal size rather than going up. These are firm-ground (FG) cleats. Where can I wear them? On dry, natural grass, which covers most league and school matches. They're not built for turf (look for the TF version), for artificial grass (the AG plate), or for an indoor court (an IC shoe). The FG studs wear down fast on hard turf, so match the cleat to your surface to keep the plate and studs intact. What's the difference between the Vapor 17 and the Superfly 11? Same Mercurial family, two different jobs as of the 2026 generation. The Vapor is the low-cut agility cleat: AtomKnit upper, FlyLite plate, built for quick cuts and winning in tight space. The Superfly is the high-collar speed cleat built for top-end, straight-line pace down the open channel. If you live on the dribble and the change of direction, the Vapor is your cleat. Is the Elite worth it over the Pro tier? The Elite is the top build, with the full AtomKnit upper and the FlyLite plate, so you get the lightest, closest-to-barefoot feel Nike makes in the Vapor. The Pro tier drops to a slightly heavier upper and plate at a lower price and still plays the same agility game. If you want the lightest touch and the sharpest cuts, the Elite is the one. Shop the Breakout Soccer Cleats Pack by Nike

items.description_en: You Set the Tempo, the Cleat Keeps Up There's a moment in every match where the ball finds you in space and the whole field opens. You can play it early and quicken everything, or hold it half a beat and make forty other players wait on you. That moment is what the Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite FG is for. It rewards the player who conducts: the deep midfielder spraying it wide, the number eight turning out of pressure, the playmaker who'd rather pass you open than run past you. Nike built the Tiempo as its touch-and-control line, and the Elite is the top of it. Why the Techleather Upper Rewards a Clean First Touch Control starts the instant the ball arrives, and a heavy first touch costs you the pass you already saw. The Techleather upper is Nike's answer: a synthetic leather that's softer than the real thing, so the ball settles where you want it and your next move is already underway. It stays sticky and consistent when the grass is wet, which matters when the Saturday field is still damp from Friday. The result is a cleat that makes a clean first touch feel automatic, so your eyes stay up and your tempo stays yours. Built for Firm Ground, Wrapped Like a Glove Firm-ground studs are cut for dry natural grass, where the bulk of league and school fixtures are played. The Maestro360 split plate sits under the forefoot and heel so the upper can wrap your arch for that glove-like fit, and bladed studs with twisted conical tips let you plant, turn, and open your body in one motion. An integrated knit collar locks the ankle without bulk. Want to compare the Pro and Academy tiers? Browse the Nike Tiempo Maestro lineup , or see the rest of this drop in the Breakout Pack . Product Details Nike Techleather upper: synthetic leather softer than natural, for a consistent touch in wet or dry conditions Maestro360 split forefoot-and-heel plate that lets the upper wrap the arch for a glove-like fit Integrated knit collar for a locked-in ankle without added bulk Bladed studs with twisted conical tips for plant-and-pivot traction on firm ground Molded surface lines on the upper to enhance touch and ball feel Firm-ground (FG) outsole for dry natural grass Low-top cut, part of the Tiempo touch-and-control silo Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack, SU26) Elite tier: Nike's top-level Tiempo Maestro build FAQs About Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite FG Soccer Cleats Does the Tiempo Maestro Elite run true to size? For most players, yes, true to size. The Techleather upper is soft from the box and molds to your foot quickly, so you don't need to size up for break-in the way old k-leather cleats demanded. If you're between sizes or have a wider midfoot, the glove-like wrap tends to forgive that better than a stiff synthetic. Try them on with your game socks. Is this real leather, and how do I break it in and care for it? It's Techleather, Nike's synthetic leather, not natural k-leather. That's good news for break-in: it's soft on day one and won't soak up water and go heavy like real leather does. Wipe the dirt off after matches, let them air dry away from direct heat, and never put them in a dryer. Stuff them with newspaper if they get soaked. These are firm-ground (FG) cleats. Where can I actually wear them? On dry, natural grass, which covers most league and school matches. They aren't made for turf (look for the TF version), for artificial grass (the AG plate), or for an indoor court (an IC shoe). FG studs wear down fast on hard turf, so match the cleat to your surface. Should I get the Tiempo Maestro or a speed cleat like the Mercurial? Depends on how you win games. If your value is pace and getting in behind, the Mercurial is the speed line. The Tiempo Maestro is for the player who controls the game through touch: receiving under pressure, turning, and dictating the pass. The Techleather upper and split plate are tuned for feel and control, not top-end sprint speed.

items.name: Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite Artificial Grass Pro Soccer Cleats - Breakout Pack (SU26)
items.description: The Touch Player Whose Home Pitch is Artificial Grass Piense en un pianista que aprende una pieza en un gran concierto, luego se sienta en un pasillo diferente en un instrumento diferente y lo toca nota por nota. Las mismas manos, la misma sensación, nueva etapa. Eso es lo que el Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite AG da al creador de juegos que vive en 3G. El toque que has construido sobre hierba no se deja en la puerta del club de césped. Dejas caer entre las líneas, tomas la bola en el medio giro, y rociarla en ancho, y la superficie debajo de ti deja de ser un compromiso. Este es el cleat para el jugador que pone el tempo de fondo, en la superficie la mayoría de los partidos de la noche de la semana se juegan en realidad. Cómo TECHLEATHER mantiene su primer toque suave en Turf Aquí está el momento que lo vende: una bola conducida llega a ritmo, lo cojín muerto, y se sienta un patio delante de usted listo para ser jugado. TECLEATHER hace que sea repetible. Es un cuero sintético que es más suave que lo real y mantiene el mismo agarre húmedo o seco, que importa cuando un lanzamiento 3G se pone grasiento bajo las luces. La placa dividida Maestro360 permite la envoltura superior del arco de tu pie, por lo que los flexiones con tu zancada en lugar de luchar contra ella. El resultado es un toque que se siente como cuero y una comodidad que se mantiene durante una temporada completa de césped. Construido para césped artificial, encerrado a través de la hierba artificial cortada (AG) es la superficie sintetica verde, no césped de la vieja escuela y no césped natural. Esta es la placa AG-Pro: más cortos, más densos cópicos propagan la carga
items.description_en: The Touch Player Whose Home Pitch Is Artificial Grass Think of a pianist who learns a piece on a concert grand, then sits down at a different hall on a different instrument and plays it note for note. Same hands, same feel, new stage. That's what the Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite AG gives the deep-lying playmaker who lives on 3G. The touch you've built on grass doesn't get left at the door of the turf club. You drop between the lines, take the ball on the half-turn, and spray it wide, and the surface under you stops being a compromise. This is the cleat for the player who sets the tempo from deep, on the surface most weeknight matches are actually played on. How TECHLEATHER Keeps Your First Touch Soft on Turf Here's the moment that sells it: a driven ball arrives at pace, you cushion it dead, and it sits a yard in front of you ready to be played. TECHLEATHER makes that repeatable. It's a synthetic leather that's softer than the real thing and holds the same grip wet or dry, which matters when a 3G pitch gets greasy under the lights. The Maestro360 split plate lets the upper wrap the arch of your foot, so the cleat flexes with your stride instead of fighting it. The result is a touch that feels like leather and a comfort that holds up over a full season of turf. Built for Artificial Grass, Locked In Through the Cut Artificial grass (AG) is the green synthetic surface, not old-school turf and not natural grass. This is the AG-Pro plate: shorter, denser conical studs spread the load across the 3G so you get grip without the studs catching the way a firm-ground sole does on synthetic. You plant, you pivot, you push off, and the surface holds. Playing mostly on natural grass instead? The same cleat comes in a firm-ground build. Compare the full silo in the Nike Tiempo Maestro collection , or browse artificial grass soccer cleats across every brand. Product Details Nike TECHLEATHER upper: synthetic leather softer than natural leather, consistent grip and touch in wet or dry conditions Maestro360 split forefoot-and-heel plate: lets the upper wrap the arch for a glove-like, flexible fit AG-Pro outsole: shorter, denser conical studs engineered for artificial grass (3G synthetic surfaces) Molded touch lines on the upper to enhance ball feel for dribbling and passing Suede-style heel liner for a locked-in heel and secure fit Elite tier: Nike's top-level Tiempo Maestro build Colorway: Ivory / Semi Blue Burst / Icey Blue (Breakout Pack, SU26) FAQs About Nike Tiempo Maestro Elite AG Cleats Are these AG cleats right for my surface, or should I get the firm-ground version? Get the AG version if you play most of your matches on artificial grass, the green synthetic 3G surface. The AG-Pro plate uses shorter conical studs that grip turf evenly and are warrantied for it, where firm-ground studs can catch and wear fast on synthetic. If your home pitch is natural grass, the Maestro Elite comes in a firm-ground (FG) build instead. Match the plate to the surface you actually play on most. Does the Tiempo Maestro Elite run true to size? For most players, true to size, with a snug rather than roomy fit through the midfoot. The TECHLEATHER upper molds to your foot over the first couple of sessions, so a close fit out of the box is normal and tends to settle in. If you have a wider foot, try them on with your match socks before committing, since the Maestro is built more for a locked-in feel than a generous toe box. TECHLEATHER on turf, how do I keep it lasting? TECHLEATHER is lower-maintenance than natural leather because it doesn't soak up water the way K-leather does. Knock the turf pellets off after a session, wipe the upper down, and let them air-dry away from direct heat. Don't machine-wash them and don't leave them baking in a hot car. Treated that way, the synthetic leather holds its touch and shape across a full turf season. Is the Maestro a control cleat or a speed cleat? A control and touch cleat, built for the player who receives, turns, and dictates rather than the one who wins games on pure pace. If top-end speed is your game, Nike's Mercurial line is the speed silo. The Tiempo Maestro is for the deep-lying playmaker who sets the tempo, and the TECHLEATHER upper is engineered for feel on the ball, not for shaving grams.

items.description: El paso hacia arriba de los pendientes del reproductor Conoces la sensación de superar tus viejos cleats: el tacto que tienes ahora merece mejor equipo que lo que te trajo aquí. El Nike Phantom 6 Low Pro FG está construido para exactamente ese jugador, el club o el playmaker de secundaria que ha ganado un cleat serio y quiere el verdadero control Phantom sin el precio Elite. Lleva el mismo Phantom DNA Nike pone a los pies de sus principales creadores, ajustado a un nivel que un jugador en desarrollo puede alcanzar. Lo encajes y la brecha entre tú y los principiantes se vuelve un poco más pequeña. Por qué VNMSkin hace que tu toque sea repetible El trabajo que hiciste en el entrenamiento sólo cuenta si aparece en el día del juego. La capa de VNMSkin agarrada se sienta sobre una base suave de Flyknit y agarra la pelota a través de la zona de huelga, así que recibir, girar y pasar todos comienzan a sentirse como el mismo movimiento confiable. Este es el nivel Pro, así que consigues ese control confiable sin pagar por la parte superior completa de Elite. El resultado es un cleat que hace el trabajo, semana y semana fuera, y permite que sus buenos hábitos viajen desde el campo de entrenamiento hasta el partido. Un bajo corte construido para el Grass seco Esta es una configuración de tierra firme (FG) para césped natural seco, la superficie bajo la mayoría de clubes y juegos escolares. La tracción Cyclone 360 de pie (el mismo patrón de soleplato que la Elite) te permite plantar y pivotar el instante en que observas la carrera. Esta es la versión baja: un tobillo estándar cortado sin collar, por lo que su pie se mueve libre y el grillete se queda fuera del camino. Quiere el mismo tier con un co
items.description_en: The Step Up the Rising Player Earns You know the feeling of outgrowing your old cleats: the touch you have now deserves better gear than what got you here. The Nike Phantom 6 Low Pro FG is built for exactly that player, the club or high-school playmaker who has earned a serious cleat and wants the real Phantom control without the Elite price. It carries the same Phantom DNA Nike puts on the feet of its top creators, tuned down to a tier a developing player can actually reach. You lace it up and the gap between you and the starters gets a little smaller. Why VNMSkin Makes Your Touch Repeatable The work you did in training only counts if it shows up on game day. The grippy VNMSkin layer sits over a soft Flyknit base and grabs the ball across the strike zone, so receiving, turning, and passing all start to feel like the same dependable motion. This is the Pro tier, so you get that trustworthy control without paying for the full Elite upper. The result is a cleat that does the job, week in and week out, and lets your good habits travel from the training ground to the match. A Low Cut Built for Dry Grass This is a firm-ground (FG) setup for dry natural grass, the surface under most club and school games. The Cyclone 360 forefoot traction (the same soleplate pattern as the Elite) lets you plant and pivot the instant you spot the run. This is the Low version: a standard ankle cut with no collar, so your foot moves free and the cleat stays out of the way. Want the same tier with a collar? Compare the High Pro and the rest of the line in the Nike Phantom collection , or see the full drop in the Breakout Pack . Product Details Nike VNMSkin: grippy layer over the strike zone for control when dribbling, passing, and shooting Flyknit base works with VNMSkin to bring your foot closer to the ball Updated shoe frame for a natural toe-box fit and closer cleat-to-ball contact Cyclone 360 circular forefoot traction for fast plant-and-pivot cuts Low-cut collar: standard ankle height, no wrap, for free movement Firm-ground (FG) outsole for dry natural grass Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack, SU26) Pro tier: Nike's mid-tier Phantom build, most of the Elite feel at a friendlier price FAQs About Nike Phantom 6 Low Pro FG Soccer Cleats What is the difference between the Phantom 6 Pro and the Elite? The Elite uses Nike's full Gripknit upper and sits at the top price. The Pro keeps the same Phantom shape and the same Cyclone 360 soleplate but swaps in a VNMSkin-over-Flyknit upper to bring the price down. You lose a little of the Elite's stickiest grip; you keep most of the control. For a developing or club player, the Pro is the value sweet spot. Does the Phantom 6 Low Pro run true to size? For most players, yes, true to size. The updated frame gives a rounder, more natural toe box than past Phantoms, so if you have a slightly wider forefoot you can usually stay at your normal size. If you wear thick game socks, try them on with those before deciding. The Low version has no collar. How does that feel? The Low is a standard ankle cut with no fabric collar, so nothing wraps or grips above the foot. Players who find a collar tight or who just prefer a free ankle tend to like the Low. If you want the locked-in collar feel instead, the Phantom 6 comes in a High Pro. These are firm-ground (FG) cleats. Where do I wear them? On dry, natural grass, which covers most club and school matches. They are not made for turf (look for the TF version), artificial grass (the AG plate), or an indoor court (an IC shoe). FG studs wear down fast on hard turf, so match the cleat to your surface.

items.name: Nike Phantom 6 High Elite Firm Ground Soccer Cleats - Breakout Pack (SU26)
items.description: The Cleat for the Player Who Decide the Game Picture the ball arrive at your feet with a defender on your shoulder, the keeper tramping to the near post, and a half-second to decide. Tomas el toque, abres tu cuerpo, y lo doblas en la esquina superior antes de que alguien lo lea. Ese momento es para lo que es el Fenómeno 6 High Elite FG de Nike. Recibe al jugador que ambos hacen la oportunidad y la toma, el número diez entrando a dictar o el futuro sosteniendo la pelota hacia arriba y girando. Nike construye el Fantasma como su línea de control, y la Elite es el nivel superior de ella. Por qué el Gripknit Upper cambia tu toque La mayoría de los acabados son sólo la repetición: la misma huelga, golpeó limpio, una y otra vez hasta que deja de ser una apuesta y comienza a ser un hábito. La parte superior Gripknit te ayuda a llegar allí. Es una textura pegajosa que se extiende por toda la parte superior, no sólo la zona de huelga, por lo que recibir, girar, gotear y disparar todos se sienten como la misma superficie confiable. Contiene el mismo mojado o seco, que importa cuando el lanzamiento del sábado todavía está empapado de la lluvia del viernes. El resultado es un cleat que hace que su buen toque repetible bajo presión. Construido para tierra firme, encerrado en el suelo firme del tobillo (FG) significa hierba seca, natural: la superficie más liga y los partidos escolares se juegan en. El patrón de tracción Cyclone 360 se sienta debajo del pie para que pueda plantar y pivotar el instante que vea la brecha. Esta es la versión alta, con un collar de fijación dinámica que envuelve el tobillo en Flyknit estirado para una cerradura
items.description_en: The Cleat for the Player Who Decides the Game Picture the ball arriving at your feet with a defender on your shoulder, the keeper cheating to the near post, and a half-second to decide. You take the touch, open your body, and bend it into the far corner before anyone reads it. That moment is what the Nike Phantom 6 High Elite FG is for. It rewards the player who both makes the chance and takes it, the number ten dropping in to dictate or the forward holding the ball up and turning. Nike builds the Phantom as its control line, and the Elite is the top tier of it. Why the Gripknit Upper Changes Your Touch Most of finishing is just repetition: the same strike, struck clean, over and over until it stops being a gamble and starts being a habit. The Gripknit upper helps you get there. It's a sticky texture spread across the whole upper, not just the strike zone, so receiving, turning, dribbling, and shooting all feel like the same reliable surface. It grips the same wet or dry, which matters when the Saturday pitch is still soaked from Friday rain. The result is a cleat that makes your good touch repeatable under pressure. Built for Firm Ground, Locked In at the Ankle Firm ground (FG) means dry, natural grass: the surface most league and school matches are played on. The Cyclone 360 traction pattern sits under the forefoot so you can plant and pivot the instant you spot the gap. This is the High version, with a Dynamic Fit collar that wraps your ankle in stretchy Flyknit for a locked-in feel through every cut. Want the same cleat without the collar? The Phantom 6 comes in a Low Elite too. Compare the full line in the Nike Phantom collection . Product Details - Nike Gripknit upper: sticky texture across the whole upper for grip and control, equal in wet or dry conditions - Dynamic Fit high collar in soft, stretchy Flyknit for a secure, locked-in ankle - Ghost Lacing system covers the laces for a cleaner strike surface - Cyclone 360 circular forefoot traction for fast plant-and-pivot cuts - Updated shoe frame for a natural toe-box fit and closer cleat-to-ball contact - Firm-ground (FG) outsole for dry natural grass - Colorway: Multi-Color / Black (Breakout Pack, SU26) - Elite tier: Nike's top-level Phantom build FAQ About Nike Phantom 6 High Elite FG Cleats Does the Phantom 6 High Elite run true to size? For most players, yes, true to size. The updated frame gives a roomier, more natural toe box than past Phantoms, so if you're between sizes or have a wider forefoot, you can usually stay at your normal size rather than going up. If you wear thick game socks, try them on with those. These are firm-ground (FG) cleats. Where can I actually wear them? On dry, natural grass, which covers most league and school matches. They are not made for turf (look for the TF version), for artificial grass (the AG plate), or for an indoor court (an IC shoe). FG studs wear down fast on hard turf, so match the cleat to your surface. What's the difference between the High Elite and the Low Elite or the Pro? The High and Low are the same Elite cleat with a different collar: High wraps your ankle in a Dynamic Fit collar, Low sits at a standard cut for players who don't want a collar. The Pro tier drops to a slightly different upper and plate build at a lower price. The Elite is the top tier, with the full Gripknit upper. Is the Phantom 6 a finishing cleat or a speed cleat? A control and finishing cleat. If you live on the shoulder of the last defender and win games with pure pace, the Mercurial is the speed line. The Phantom is for the player who receives, turns, and releases: the one who shapes the play and picks the corner. The Gripknit upper is built for touch and precision, not top-end speed.

Es sesiones de pequeño lado bajo las luces, superficies de entrenamiento 3G y 4G, la jaula en un martes, una corte de césped duro donde la bola se mueve más rápido y así lo haces tú. items.description_en: The control player who lives on turf Your week isn't ninety minutes on a manicured pitch. It's small-sided sessions under the lights, 3G and 4G training surfaces, the cage on a Tuesday, a hard turf court where the ball moves quicker and so do you. That's where touch wins, and where most cleats give up the feel you need. The adidas Predator Pro turf shoe is built for the committed competitive player who calls that surface home. Pro is the serious-amateur tier, one rung under the Elite. You get the Predator's control DNA tuned for hard ground, where the studs are short and many and your feet stay quick in tight spaces. Pro-tier control, turf-specific build The Predator name has stood for one thing across three decades: putting more of the ball on your foot. This is the Pro reading of that idea, sized for turf. Nanostrike Pro layers an innovative mesh with integrated haptic areas across the strike zone, so the ball grips when you clip a pass in traffic or wrap your laces around a shot from the top of the box. Powerspine through the midfoot keeps the platform stable when you plant and turn on a hard surface, and Lightstrike cushioning underfoot gives you energy back over a long session. The fold-over tongue, standard at this tier, smooths the laces into one clean striking face. The synthetic and textile upper sheds the scuffs that turf hands out, and a dense pattern of short studs on the synthetic outsole keeps you planted on 3G, 4G, and worn astroturf without the grab of a firm-ground plate. Who the Predator Pro turf is for Reach for this if your soccer happens on turf and you want real control, not a stripped-down trainer. It suits the small-sided regular, the futsal-adjacent winger, the player who trains midweek on artificial surfaces and wants the same touch they'd get on grass. Browse the rest of the adidas Predator range if you also play firm ground or artificial grass and want the matching plate. The Road to Glory Pack carries this colorway across the 2026 line. Product Details: Predator Pro Turf Synthetic and textile upper that resists turf scuffing Fold-over tongue for a smooth, lace-free striking surface Nanostrike Pro mesh with integrated haptic areas across the strike zone Powerspine midfoot for stability on hard surfaces Lightstrike cushioning for energy return over long sessions Synthetic turf outsole with a dense pattern of short studs Synthetic sockliner, regular fit, lace closure Weight: 8.8 oz (249g) Fit Notes Runs true to size for most players. If you're between sizes or have a narrow foot, dropping a half size gives you the snug, locked-in feel the Predator line is built for. Wider feet sit comfortably at true size with little to no break-in. Care and Maintenance Knock the turf pellets and dirt loose with a soft brush after every session Air-dry at room temperature; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them clear of direct heat, sun, and dryers, which can warp the outsole Wipe the synthetic upper with a damp cloth; the mesh doesn't need conditioner FAQs about the Predator Pro Turf What surface is the Predator Pro turf shoe built for? It's a turf (TF) shoe, made for artificial turf and hard surfaces: 3G and 4G training pitches, small-sided cages, worn astroturf. The synthetic outsole uses a dense pattern of short studs instead of the longer studs you'd find on a firm-ground plate, which keeps your footing on hard ground. How does the Pro compare to the Predator Elite? The Pro is the serious-amateur tier, one step below the Elite. It carries the same control idea, with Nanostrike Pro on the strike zone, Powerspine midfoot stability, and the fold-over tongue, at a more accessible price. The Elite adds a higher-spec upper and plate for the top tier. If you want most of the Predator control feel without the Elite outlay, the Pro is the pick. Does the Predator Pro turf run true to size? It does for most players. For a narrow foot or a tighter, more locked-in fit, drop a half size. Wider feet fit well at true size and need little break-in. Can I wear these on natural grass? You can on a kickabout, but it's not what they're for. The short-stud turf outsole is tuned for artificial and hard surfaces. For natural grass you'd want the firm-ground (FG) version, and matching the outsole to your surface protects both your footing and the shoe.

items.description_en: Your pitch is turf, so your shoe should be too Your soccer doesn't happen on a manicured grass field with a groundskeeper. It happens on turf: the 3G and 4G surfaces behind the rec center, the small-sided cage with the high fence, the hard court where the winter league runs. The adidas Predator League turf shoe is built for that reality. Dependable Predator control on the surface you actually play on, priced for someone who plays every week. Predator control, tuned for the value player on turf The Predator name has stood for ball control for three decades, and the League tier brings that DNA down to an everyday build. A synthetic and textile upper with Nanostrike+ lays rubber grip elements across the strike zone, so the ball still grabs your foot when you push a pass or take a touch in traffic. The turf outsole runs many short rubber studs that bite into 3G and 4G without the stab of a firm-ground plate, and the fold-over tongue tucks the laces away for a cleaner contact surface. Who the Predator League turf is for This is the value-tier turf shoe for the regular amateur: weeknight leagues, small-sided games, and turf training when the grass is closed. You're not chasing a pro contract, you just want a shoe that grips, controls, and holds up through a full season of midweek fixtures without costing a paycheck. If you want genuine Predator feel without the Elite-tier price, and your game lives on artificial surfaces, this is the pair to grab. The Road to Glory colorway carries the adidas Road to Glory Pack look into the 2026 season. Product Details: Predator League Turf Synthetic and textile upper Fold-over tongue for a clean, lace-free striking surface Nanostrike+ with rubber grip elements across the strike zone Powerspine midfoot stability Strikeframe for traction on quick turns Turf (TF) rubber outsole with non-removable studs for 3G and 4G Textile sockliner, regular fit, lace closure Weight: 9 oz (254g) Fit Notes Runs true to size for most players. If you're between sizes or have a narrow foot, dropping a half size gives you the locked-in feel the Predator is built for. Wider feet sit comfortably at true size. Care and Maintenance Brush off turf pellets and dirt with a soft brush after every session before they pack into the studs Air-dry at room temperature; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them away from direct heat, sun, and dryers, which break down the synthetic upper and warp the outsole Wipe the upper with a damp cloth; the synthetic and Nanostrike+ mesh need no conditioner FAQs about the Predator League Turf Are these turf shoes or firm-ground cleats? These are turf (TF) shoes, built for artificial surfaces. The outsole runs many short rubber studs that grip 3G and 4G turf, small-sided cages, and hard courts. For natural grass you'd want the firm-ground (FG) version with a studded plate instead. How is the League different from the Elite Predator turf? The League is the value tier: a synthetic and textile upper with Nanostrike+, Powerspine, and the Strikeframe outsole, at an everyday price. The adidas Predator line steps up from there to Pro and Elite builds with higher-end uppers and a higher price. If you play weekly on turf and want real Predator control without the flagship cost, the League is the right call. Does the Predator League turf run true to size? It runs true to size for most players. If you have a narrow foot or want a snug, locked-in feel, drop a half size. Wider feet fit well at true size with no break-in needed.

items.description_en: The control cleat for the player who shows up every week You're not chasing a pro contract. You're the one who turns up rain or shine, plays the full ninety, and still wants the ball to do exactly what your foot tells it to. The adidas Predator League FG is built for you: real grip on the strike zone, a stable platform underfoot, and a price that makes sense for a cleat you'll actually wear into the ground. This is the senior League build, the dependable choice for the committed amateur on natural grass. It carries the Predator control identity into a tier you can afford to replace each season, so you spend less time worrying about your cleats and more time picking out passes. Predator control, carried down to the League tier Predator has stood for strike and control for three decades, and that DNA runs through the League build. A Nanostrike mesh upper layers an integrated haptic overlay across the front of the foot, so the ball grips when you strike it and sits down when you receive it. The fold-over tongue covers the laces for one smooth striking surface from instep to toe, the classic Predator touch that started this whole line. Underfoot, a full-length Strikeframe plate keeps traction reliable on firm grass, and a Powerspine through the midfoot stiffens the platform when you lean into a driven ball. It steps down from the Elite tier in materials, not intent. Who the Predator League FG is for This is a firm ground cleat, tuned for natural grass and well-kept pitches. If your league plays Sunday mornings on real turf and you want genuine control without paying for the top-tier upper, this is the build to reach for. It suits the regular weekend player, the amateur midfielder or forward who lives off touch and timing. The Road to Glory colorway pulls the look into the 2026 cycle, and it sits alongside the rest of the Road to Glory Pack if you want to match the kit. Product Details: Predator League FG Nanostrike mesh upper with integrated haptic overlay across the strike zone Fold-over tongue for a clean, lace-free striking surface Powerspine midfoot for stability on driven shots Full-length Strikeframe firm-ground plate Synthetic outsole, textile sockliner Regular fit, lace closure Weight: 8.2 oz (232g) Fit Notes Runs true to size for most players. If you're between sizes or have a narrow foot, going down a half size gives you the locked-in feel Predator is built for. Wider feet fit comfortably at true size with no break-in needed. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to hold shape and pull moisture Keep them away from direct heat, sun, and dryers, which warp the Strikeframe plate Brush off dried grass and dirt with a soft brush before they go back in the bag Wipe the Nanostrike mesh upper with a damp cloth; it does not need conditioner FAQs about the Predator League FG Does the Predator League fold-over tongue FG run true to size? It runs true to size for most players. If you have a narrow foot or want a snug, locked-in fit, drop a half size. Wider feet fit well at true size with no break-in needed. What is the difference between the Predator League and the Predator Elite? The League is the value tier: a Nanostrike mesh upper, the fold-over tongue, a Strikeframe plate, and Powerspine midfoot support, at an accessible price. The Elite sits at the top of the Predator line with a Primeknit upper and a more advanced strike zone. The League gives you genuine Predator control for the regular weekend player without the flagship cost. Are these good for artificial grass or turf? No. This is the firm ground (FG) version, built for natural grass and well-maintained pitches. For artificial grass you would want the AG plate, and for turf you would want a dedicated turf shoe. Matching the plate to your surface protects both the cleat and your footing. Is the fold-over tongue better than a standard laced cleat? It is a different feel, not strictly better. The fold-over tongue covers the laces for one clean striking surface across the instep, which control players tend to prefer. If you like the laces exposed and a more traditional setup, a standard-laced cleat is the one to look at.

items.description_en: A clean surface, every time you strike it The adidas Predator Elite Laceless is built for the player who controls a match with their feet, not their pace. No laces cross the top, so the spot where you meet the ball is one unbroken surface. Whip a cross to the back post or thread a pass between two defenders, and you feel the same contact every time. Just you, the strike, and the result. This is the Road to Glory Pack colorway in Solar Turbo, Thermal Chrome, and Core Black. Built around the laceless commitment Going laceless is a decision adidas builds the whole cleat around. The engineered Primeknit collar wraps your ankle like a sock and locks the foot in without a lace to cinch. Up front, Nanostrike+ mesh keeps the strike zone featherlight and gives the ball a true, predictable grip on contact. The Powerspine through the midfoot lets you plant and drive through a shot, and the Strikeframe plate keeps traction light on firm ground. For the full lineup, including the laced adidas Predator Elite that runs alongside it, browse the adidas Predator collection . Who reaches for the laceless Elite The adidas Predator Elite Laceless is the cleat for the controlling striker and the playmaker who lives around the ball. If you strike across the laces and have always wished that part of the cleat were smoother, this is the answer adidas wrote for you. It belongs on firm natural grass, where the Strikeframe studs bite cleanly. See the rest of the Road to Glory Pack . Product Details Tier: Predator Elite (adidas top-tier Predator) Surface: Firm Ground (FG), natural grass Upper: synthetic and textile, Nanostrike+ mesh strike zone Striking technology: Nanostrike+ for a featherlight, true-grip contact surface Stability: Powerspine through the midfoot for plant-and-drive power Plate: Strikeframe, lightweight FG traction Closure: laceless, engineered Primeknit collar Lining: synthetic Weight: 6.6 oz (187.5 g), UK 8.5 reference Colorway: Road to Glory Pack, Solar Turbo / Thermal Chrome / Core Black Fit Notes Laceless cleats fit closer than laced ones because the knit holds your foot. The Predator Elite Laceless runs true to size for most players. Wider feet or high insteps may want a half size up while the Primeknit collar settles. If you sit between sizes, go up rather than down; you cannot open a laceless cleat the way you ease a lace. Care and Maintenance Air-dry after every match; stuff with newspaper to draw out moisture and hold the collar's shape Keep them off direct heat, dryers, and a hot car; store around 70°F (21°C) Brush dried grass and dirt off the Nanostrike+ mesh before storing Synthetic upper, so no conditioner needed; a damp cloth keeps it clean Ease the collar on and off gently to keep the Primeknit from stretching FAQs about the Predator Elite Laceless Why choose the laceless Elite over the laced Predator Elite? Pick the laceless if you want one clean, unbroken surface where you strike the ball. The laced Elite gives you on-the-fly tightness adjustment; the laceless trades that for a smoother contact patch and a sock-like collar that locks the foot through the knit instead of a lace. If your game is built on the quality of your touch and your striking, the laceless is the one. Do laceless cleats stay secure without a lace? Yes. The engineered Primeknit collar and the snug knit upper hold the foot in place, and the Powerspine keeps the midfoot stable through hard cuts and shots. Most players find the lockdown feels more uniform than a laced cleat because there is no pressure point along the laces. What surface is the Predator Elite Laceless made for? Firm natural grass. The Strikeframe plate and stud pattern are built for dry, firm pitches. For artificial grass or soft, wet ground, look at the AG or SG options in the Predator line instead. How should the laceless fit compared to a laced cleat? Closer and more sock-like. They run true to size for most feet. Wider feet or high insteps may prefer a half size up, since there is no lace to open up. When in doubt, size up rather than down. Is the Road to Glory Pack colorway the same cleat as the standard Elite Laceless? Yes, same Predator Elite Laceless construction underneath. The Road to Glory Pack is the Solar Turbo, Thermal Chrome, and Core Black colorway treatment; the Nanostrike+ strike zone, Primeknit collar, Powerspine, and Strikeframe plate are unchanged.
